alerts.reason: September net sales rose 3.9% because a 16.1% increase in average unit price offset a 10.5% decline in units (A, B, D). I expect pricing to keep December sales growth above -5%. If the unit decline persists, average price growth of 6% in January–March would imply a 5.1% net sales decline.

Quarterly revenue growth fell from 4.13% in June to -1.33% in September. Growth in Sample Management Solutions and Multiomics partly offset the fiscal-year revenue decline at B Medical Systems (A, D). I expect those gains to keep December above -5%, with January–March crossing if the offset continues to weaken.

September consolidated sales grew 3.6%, helped by pricing and Americas equipment sales, while organic sales fell in EMEA and APAC (A, C). Backlog fell from $186.2 million in December 2023 to $76.8 million in September 2024 (B). I expect remaining orders to support December sales growth above -5%, with fewer orders on hand to sustain shipments in January–March.

The consolidated sales decline widened from 1.29% in June to 3.86% in September (A). September backlog was still $475.8 million, but it was $138.9 million lower than a year earlier (C). I expect outstanding orders to keep the December decline under 5%, then the smaller backlog to push the January–March decline to at least 5%.

The consolidated revenue decline widened from 1.03% in June to 3.73% in September. Applebee’s domestic same-restaurant sales fell 5.9% in September versus 4.1% over nine months, and franchise and rental revenue had already fallen (A, B). I expect consolidated revenue to remain above -5% in December and cross in January–March as weaker restaurant sales continue to weigh on franchise revenue.

Consolidated revenue growth slowed from 4.92% in June to -0.29% in September. The truckload fleet averaged 8% more tractors and earned more freight revenue per mile, but utilization fell and Managed Freight faced softer volumes (A, B, E). I expect fleet growth to cushion December, with January–March revenue down at least 5% if weaker utilization erodes that benefit.

The consolidated revenue decline narrowed from 6.51% in June to 3.02% in September (A). Contractual rate increases offset lower utilization and more idle equipment (C). I expect those rates to keep December above -5%, with persistent idle capacity putting January–March revenue back at least 5% below the prior year.

The consolidated revenue decline widened from 2.21% in June to 2.68% in September (A). Both revenue per brokerage order and volume fell, reducing Logistics revenue excluding fuel surcharges by $12.3 million, and Truckload owner-operator capacity contracted (B, C). I expect a December decline under 5%, followed by a January–March decline of at least 5% if those pressures persist.
